intent: The paragraph that states what confirming an alert dialog will do, read out as the popup's description.
typical_uses: The consequence of a confirmation, such as "This cannot be undone."

dont_use_when.situation: The description of a dismissible modal

invariants.text: AlertDialogDescription renders a p in the body type ramp with the muted foreground color.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the description's state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property; the primitive passes an empty state object.

style.states: style accepts a function as well as a plain style object; the primitive passes that function an empty state object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)`, and the description's state carries no fields. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through alert-dialog.module.css, not through this.

good.title: The consequence under the question
good.code:
<AlertDialogHeader>
  <AlertDialogTitle>Delete this project?</AlertDialogTitle>
  <AlertDialogDescription>Its files and history are removed for everyone.</AlertDialogDescription>
</AlertDialogHeader>

bad.title: A list nested in the description
bad.why: The description renders a p, and a list inside a paragraph is invalid HTML; keep the description to a sentence of text.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, DialogDescriptionState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the description's state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property; the primitive passes an empty state object.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: DialogDescriptionState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function as well as a plain style object; the primitive passes that function an empty state object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)`, and the description's state carries no fields. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through alert-dialog.module.css, not through this.
